newsitem.title: SPAIN: Guatemala's Arzu starts bid for funds in Spain.
newsitem.headline: Guatemala's Arzu starts bid for funds in Spain.

text.p: Guatemala's President Alvaro Arzu began a diplomatic offensive on Sunday to drum up international funds and attract much needed investment to his country after more than three decades of civil war.

"We are not only looking for cooperation but also the opening up of markets and a more fluid commerce that will allow Guatemalans to move forward," Arzu told a news conference during a visit to Madrid.

Arzu is on a week-long European tour to promote Guatemala's plans to implement ambitious promises contained in a peace treaty signed on December 29 between the government and the leftist Guatemalan National Revolutionary Unit (URNG) rebels.
"Now comes the great challenge to start the development process in our country," he said.

The Guatemalan government has calculated that it needs some $2.5 billion for programmes to modernise the state, combat poverty and resettle hundreds of thousands of Guatemalans displaced during 36 years of conflict.

"We are not seeking to obtain everything from the international community, either in loans or donations from friendly countries or multilateral credit organisations," Arzu said, declining to specify exactly how much he expected to collect from the international community.
However, Guatemalan diplomatic sources told Reuters that Guatemala hoped it could raise some $1.7 billion in cooperation and soft loans.
Arzu said the priority after peace was economic recovery in a country that is in desperate need of social and infrastructure investment, largely abandoned during the civil war.

During his visit to Spain, Arzu said he would also try to revive bilateral relations with Spain, which cooled after Guatemalan security forces stormed and burned the Spanish embassy in Guatemala City in 1980.
"Today the objective will be to reactivate a spirit of cooperation and commercial revival," he said.

Arzu was due to meet Spain's Prime Minister Jose Maria Aznar on Sunday night. Aznar, who attended the peace ceremony in Guatemala, has promised to increase cooperation with Guatemala and seek support from European Union members for the peace process.
Spain strongly supported Guatemala's peace efforts from the beginning of negotiations and has offered $16 million to help finance the peace agreement, diplomatic sources say.
On Monday, Arzu will lunch with Spain's King Juan Carlos and visit parliament before leaving for Brussels.
